stimulus.body: The electorate roughly doubled after 1832, though it still included only a minority of adult men. Growth was concentrated in boroughs and among middle-class householders.

questions.stem: A source note on the Reform Act of 1832 reads: "The franchise expanded but remained limited to a minority of adult men" Using that evidence, what it shows?

options.text: The electorate shrank after 1832
options.misconception: confuses The electorate shrank after 1832 with the supported claim The franchise expanded but remained limited to a minority of….

options.text: All adult men gained the vote
options.misconception: mistakes All adult men gained the vote for The franchise expanded but remained limited to a minority of….

options.text: The franchise expanded but remained limited to a minority of adult men
No new voters were added
options.misconception: denies growth

questions.explanation: The electorate grew but stayed limited. Universal male suffrage was not achieved, growth occurred, and new voters were added.

questions.subject: EUROPEAN_HISTORY
questions.learningObjective: Explain Owen's critique of competition

stimulus.body: Source note: He believed competition produced poverty and vice, while cooperation produced harmony. This is the claim the evidence in the topic supports.

questions.stem: A source note on owen's model village reads: "He believed competition produced poverty and vice, while cooperation produced harmony" Using that evidence, why Owen opposed competitive individualism?

options.text: He was indifferent to economic organisation
options.misconception: denies his concern

options.text: He believed competition always maximised welfare
options.misconception: mistakes He believed competition always maximised welfare for He believed competition produced poverty and vice, while….

options.text: He supported extreme individualism
options.misconception: reads the evidence as He supported extreme individualism instead of He believed competition produced poverty and vice, while….

options.text: He believed competition produced poverty and vice, while cooperation produced harmony

questions.explanation: Owen opposed competition as producing poverty and vice, favouring cooperation. He did not praise competition, individualism, or indifference.

questions.subject: EUROPEAN_HISTORY
questions.learningObjective: Explain how Chartism built on earlier movements

stimulus.body: Source note: It carried forward demands for political representation that earlier reformers had raised. This is the claim the evidence in the topic supports.

questions.stem: A source note on formation of the working class reads: "It carried forward demands for political representation that earlier reformers had raised" Using that evidence, how Chartism connected to earlier working-class movements?

options.text: It carried forward demands for political representation that earlier reformers had raised
It rejected all earlier reform demands
options.misconception: denies continuity

options.text: It was entirely unrelated to earlier movements
options.misconception: denies connection

options.text: It opposed political reform altogether
options.misconception: reads the evidence as It opposed political reform altogether instead of It carried forward demands for political representation that….

questions.explanation: Chartism continued earlier reform demands. It did not reject them, was connected, and sought political reform.
